{{nihongo|'''Moro Shrine'''|茂侶神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ōmononushi|fr|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|mni|ꯑꯣꯃꯣꯅꯣꯅꯨꯁꯤ|ru|Омононуси|simple|Ōmononushi|zh|大物主|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto}}（おおものぬしのみこと）

=== History ===
In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as "{{ill|Shimōsa Province|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆسا|cs|Provincie Šimósa|de|Provinz Shimousa|es|Provincia de Shimōsa|fa|ولایت شیموسا|fr|Province de Shimōsa|gl|Provincia de Shimōsa|hak|Shimōsa-koet|id|Provinsi Shimousa|it|Shimōsa|ja|下総国|ko|시모사국|lt|Šimosos žemė|nl|Shimosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimōsa|ru|Симоса (провинция)|simple|Shimōsa Province|sk|Šimósa|sr|Провинција Шимоса|tr|Shimōsa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоса|zh|下總國|zh_min_nan|Simôsa-kok|zh_yue|下總國|qid=Q1053695}}{{ill|Katsushika district|de|Katsushika-gun|ja|葛飾郡|ko|가쓰시카군|zh|葛飾郡|qid=Q11621089}} Moro Shrine" as a small shrine, and is regarded as one candidate shrine. There are two other candidate shrines (in {{ill|Matsudo|Q320943|qid=Q320943}} and {{ill|Funabashi|Q271417|qid=Q271417}})（see "{{ill|Moro Shrine|Q11617025|qid=Q11617025}}"）.
The first appearance of Moro Shrine itself in the national chronicles is in the entry for 12 November, Jōgan 13 (817), in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}: "Moro-no-kami was granted {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} Senior Fifth Rank, Upper." Later, on 25 September, Gangyō 3（{{ill|879|Q25001|qid=Q25001}}）, it was granted Senior Fifth Rank, Upper.

The founding of the shrine is unknown. Its deity Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto is considered a divided spirit from {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}} on {{ill|Mount Miwa|Q860627|qid=Q860627}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}, and the shrine name "Moro" is thought to come from "Moro" in the old name of Mt. Miwa, "Mimoro-yama."<ref>There is also a theory that it derives from "mori," meaning a sacred grove where gods dwell.</ref> For this reason, the plateau where the shrine stands is also called "Mt. Miwa"（{{ill|Miwano-yama|ja|三輪野山|qid=Q11357427}}）. From remains of a jingū-ji, old torii remains on the former western approach at Hirai, and place-name origins such as Yagi-gō, it is inferred that the shrine once had an extensive {{ill|shin'iki|Q11588853|qid=Q11588853}}.

In {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 3（{{ill|1598|Q6800|qid=Q6800}}）, excavation of the {{ill|Edo River|Q1194505|qid=Q1194505}} divided the sacred area. This shrine lies on the east bank. As a result, during the {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} era a branch shrine was established on the west bank, and {{ill|Miwa Shrine|Q119929491|qid=Q119929491|lt=Miwa Shrine}} was founded. Also, the shrine received an annual offering of 25 koku from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|Q205662|qid=Q205662}}.

=== Precincts ===
* Honden
* Haiden - the roof tiles were re-laid in Heisei 7.

Adjacent to the precincts are remains of a {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}.

=== Ritual ===
* Jingara-mochi
: At the Obisha (New Year rite) on {{ill|January 8|Q2234|qid=Q2234}}, kagami-mochi is offered before the deity and then parishioners tear it apart. The way it breaks was used to divine the year's harvest. It is designated by {{ill|Nagareyama|ar|ناغاره ياما (تشيبا)|azb|ناقاریاما، چیبا|ce|Нагареяма|ceb|Nagareyama (distrito)|cs|Nagarejama|de|Nagareyama|eo|Nagarejama|es|Nagareyama (Chiba)|fa|ناگاریاما، چیبا|fi|Nagareyama|fr|Nagareyama|gl|Nagareyama|he|נגריאמה|id|Nagareyama, Chiba|it|Nagareyama|ja|流山市|ko|나가레야마시|mg|Nagareyama|mzn|ناگاریاما، چیبا|nl|Nagareyama|no|Nagareyama|pl|Nagareyama|pt|Nagareyama|ro|Nagareyama|ru|Нагареяма|sh|Nagarejama|sr|Нагарејама|sv|Nagareyama|sw|Nagareyama, Chiba|tg|Нагареяма|th|นางาเรยามะ|tl|Nagareyama|tr|Nagareyama|tt|Нагареяма|tum|Nagareyama|uk|Наґареяма|ur|ناگارییاما، چیبا|uz|Nagareyama|vi|Nagareyama, Chiba|war|Nagareyama|zh|流山市|zh_classical|流山市|zh_min_nan|Nagareyama-chhī|zh_yue|流山|qid=Q328625}} as an intangible folk cultural property.
